summary: Regression test for the 'identical feedback / identical 3/5 scores' bug in the Interview Practice flow. Bug is FIXED. Backend: 8/8 pytest cases pass against POST /api/interview/evaluate — strong, mid, and weak answers to the same question return differentiated scores (strong technical > weak), non-identical feedback text, and response-specific bullets (e.g., quotes 'Gordon', 'perpetuity', '1,428'). Frontend: logged in as testagent2026@gmail.com, went to /session/5e0c2a88-d864-4827-9a95-5aedd8d27ffd/interview, submitted 3 different-quality answers. Network panel confirms 3x POST /api/interview/evaluate -> 200 (LLM path hit, NOT template fallback). Scores rendered by UI differ across answers: STRONG Technical 4/5, Clarity 3/5, Structure 4/5, Overall 4/5 vs WEAK 1/5, 2/5, 1/5, 1/5. Every strengths/improvements bullet is specific and references concrete content from the candidate's answer (e.g., 'Correctly identified opportunity cost and inflation', 'Strong connection to practical applications: DCF, bond pricing, NPV'). LLM also demonstrated cross-question awareness — called out when a candidate's answer did not address the actual question asked. Evaluating… spinner stays visible during LLM call (~6-8s). No console errors during flow. End-to-end Submit -> LLM -> feedback card -> Next wiring works per question.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py evaluate_interview_response: clamp() defaults invalid/missing numeric fields to 1 (the lower bound). If the LLM ever omits one score entirely, the candidate gets a silent 1/5 — consider logging when a key is missing vs letting it pass as a real low score.
INTERVIEW_EVAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the model to 'Return ONLY the JSON object. No code fences.' but the endpoint still strips ``` fences defensively. Good resilience; keep it.

InterviewPage.jsx evaluateWithLLM has a 30s axios timeout. Observed LLM p95 was ~7-8s, so 30s is safe, but there is no user-visible retry or 'taking longer than usual' nudge — template fallback triggers silently on any failure. Consider a toast when fallback path fires so the user / support can tell signal apart from LLM output.

Frontend UI labels the score pill as 'CLARITY' while backend returns the key 'communication'. Mapping is done inside the component correctly today, but the terminology mismatch is a minor foot-gun for future refactors — align either the API key or the pill label.

handleSubmit sets phase='evaluating' before the LLM call but does not guard against double-click/double-submit between the click and the axios promise resolution (canSubmit flips because phase changes, so in practice it's safe — worth a one-line comment so a future edit doesn't break it).

context_for_next_testing_agent: LLM-backed interview evaluator is live and healthy. Row user_sessions.id=5e0c2a88-d864-4827-9a95-5aedd8d27ffd still has interview_completed=false / interview_score=null (we stopped after Q3 feedback, never reached the complete page). Test file /app/backend/tests/test_interview_evaluate.py hits the real Emergent LLM and costs ~3 Claude Sonnet calls per run — rerun only when prompt or endpoint contract changes. Observed LLM latency: ~5-8s per call; 30s axios timeout has plenty of headroom. No frontend changes required.
rca of the issue: Original bug: evaluation_criteria JSONB in Supabase uses keys must_cover/bonus_points/red_flags but the template evaluator (interviewEval.js) only looked at keywords/key_points -> every answer hit the same default path -> identical 3/5 scores and generic feedback. Fix (already applied by main agent): backend POST /api/interview/evaluate endpoint built on Claude Sonnet via Emergent LLM Key with a strict-JSON contract; frontend awaits it as primary path with template evaluator kept as a pure fallback. Verified via 3 different-quality submissions producing 3 different score/feedback sets that quote candidate phrasing directly.
